narration: Here's something wild — you can earn more and actually take home less. It's not a tax bracket myth. It's a benefit cliff, and millions of people are standing right on one without knowing it.
visual: Person silhouette receives a 'YOU GOT A RAISE +$2,000' notification on a phone, but the wallet behind them drains to empty. Text overlay: 'MORE PAY = LESS MONEY?' in bold white.

narration: If your income is under 400% of the federal poverty line, you qualify for health insurance subsidies worth thousands. Earn one dollar over that line and the government claws back every cent. Zero. Gone.
visual: Person silhouette walking toward a cliff labeled '400% FPL = $58,320/yr'. Dollar signs float upward and away as the person reaches the edge. Light background.

narration: For a single person in 2026, that cliff sits at $58,320. Earn $58,321 and you lose around $3,200 a year in subsidies. Your employer gave you a raise — the government immediately took $3,200 more.
visual: Side-by-side comparison: left box '$58,320' with green border and '+$3,200 SUBSIDY'. Right box '$58,321' with red border and '-$3,200 NO SUBSIDY'. Center shows '+$1 →' arrow. Dark background.

narration: And it's not just health insurance. SNAP food benefits, Medicaid, housing vouchers, and childcare subsidies all have their own cliffs. Stack them together and one promotion can cost you over twelve thousand dollars a year.
visual: Four benefit cards sliding in one by one: HEALTH ($3,200), FOOD ($2,100), HOUSING ($4,800), CHILDCARE ($2,400). Total box at bottom shows '-$12,500'. Light background.

narration: Over fifty million Americans live near at least one benefit cliff. The fix isn't turning down the raise — it's knowing your numbers first. A raise smaller than your benefit loss is a pay cut disguised as good news.
visual: Grid of 50 small person silhouettes, the right column highlighted in red near a dotted cliff line. Text: '50 MILLION AT RISK'. Then: 'A RAISE SMALLER THAN YOUR LOSS IS A PAY CUT'. Dark background.

narration: Before you say yes to your next raise, search 'benefit cliff calculator' — they're completely free. Know what income level keeps you whole. Because more money on paper doesn't always mean more money in your pocket.
visual: Phone screen showing a search bar typing out 'benefit cliff calculator', then search results appearing with free tools. CTA text: 'SEARCH: BENEFIT CLIFF CALCULATOR'. Light background.
